name: _Organized Desktop/02 Build Projects/buildantigVG
top_fix: Copy checks/workforce/*.json+logs into astraupskill/evidence/ so the 37-check claim is verifiable from inside the repo, and add a 'break it' chapter (remove version from the updateMany where-clause, remove tenantId from get) so the course has a predict-run-verify loop.
summary: Empty NestJS module turned into a real tenant-scoped worker directory: scrypt sign-in, request-time account/tenant revocation checks, optimistic concurrency via version-conditional updateMany with an affected-row check, lifecycle guards, audit inside the same transaction, composite (companyId,tenantId) FK, and a per-tenant unique email. Uniquely strong evidence: 29 Jest tests over supertest against a disposable PostgreSQL 18 cluster the harness creates and destroys, including a rollback test that installs a real failing trigger on AuditLog, plus 8 Playwright scenarios and reviewed screenshots of the running app. Weaknesses are pedagogical: no break-it-then-fix-it loop, and all five practice exercises are open-ended mid-level design tasks with review heuristics instead of solutions.

name: _Organized Desktop/03 Master Projects/master2
top_fix: Add a disposable-PostgreSQL integration test that forces the audit write to fail mid-transaction and races two identical providerEventIds; today Serializable isolation, rollback and the P2002/P2034 retry loop are only asserted against vi.fn(). Also state that a real webhook cannot present tenant headers, so production must derive the tenant from a verified signature.
summary: Extracts the mock payment webhook into a service that checks payments:manage, hashes the payload for event identity, rejects a provider event owned by another tenant or carrying different contents, scopes payment/invoice reads by organizationId, guards the invoice transition, refuses to regress a succeeded payment on a late failure, and wraps it in a Serializable transaction with bounded retries; plus a DomainError/HttpError hierarchy replacing an error handler that picked HTTP status by substring-matching exception messages. Real bugs fixed (the old webhook updated payment by id with no tenant predicate; the payments list included organizationId: null rows). 30 tests assert query predicates and the absence of writes, but Prisma is mocked throughout and four chapters inline their own solutions.

name: _Organized Desktop/03 Master Projects/master3
top_fix: Add tests/integration/ticket-patch.int.test.ts against a disposable Postgres asserting auditLog/outboxEvent counts are unchanged after each viewer PATCH shape and +1 after an agent PATCH; and either add P2034 retry handling or drop the newly-added Serializable isolation the course teaches but never tests.
summary: Moves the ticket-edit role check to the first line of updateTicket so a VIEWER PATCH (including {}, tags-only, priority-only) is rejected before any Prisma lookup, and makes the PATCH response reuse the same role-aware comment include as GET so a successful update can no longer leak INTERNAL comments. The lesson - a partial body is still one authorized operation, and response shaping is part of the endpoint contract - transfers directly to any Node/Prisma API. The new tests assert the ordering property (findFirst and $transaction never called) rather than just status codes, and VERIFICATION.md is blunt that all 14 tests mock Prisma. Never shows the learner how to boot the app or the database.

name: _Organized Desktop/03 Master Projects/master4
top_fix: Add tests/reservation-api.test.ts using the existing supertest+seeded-SQLite setup to POST /api/orders/:id/reserve with two lines for one SKU and assert HTTP 200 ok:false plus unchanged inventoryItem.reserved and stockReservation counts; and make orders.service.ts actually call applyReservation (its new guards are currently dead code).
summary: Fixes a real oversell: planReservation compared each order line against the same stock pool independently, so lines of 14 and 9 both 'fit' in 22 available units. The repair groups demand by skuId before comparing and rejects non-positive/fractional/non-finite quantities. Pedagogically the best in the batch - Exercise 1 makes you reproduce the oversell as a failing test against the shipped pre-change snapshot before touching source, and solutions live in a separate file. Verification is exemplary: it volunteers that the focused 9-test run is a subset, that the three DB-backed tests never hit the reservation endpoint, and that a rejected reservation still writes an audit row. Narrow scope: one pure function, no authz or pagination content.

name: _Organized Desktop/03 Master Projects/master7
top_fix: Fix the broken link Astra added to the root README.md line 13 (docs/code-walkthroughs/audit-log-scope/README.md does not exist), and extract one shared auditLogScope(actor) predicate used by both visibleAuditLogs and services.auditLogs instead of two copies of the same rule.
summary: The dedicated /audit-logs endpoint was already tenant-scoped, but a second projection on the dashboard was not - so an Acme admin saw Nova's audit rows whenever they landed in the global first 25. The fix filters by organizationId before slice(0,25), and the best idea in the course is exactly that ordering: filter by owner before applying the page limit, or a noisy tenant eats your first page. The regression test is a real HTTP test (server.listen(0) + fetch) asserting all three role arms. Honest that its 'database' is an in-memory object and that a Prisma schema sitting elsewhere in the repo proves nothing. No writes, transactions or DB anywhere in the lesson, and four of five exercises are prediction-only.

name: grokbuildecommerceproject
top_fix: Ship checks/commerce-workspace/full-final/*.json and logs inside astraupskill/evidence/, and add a 03b-BREAK-IT chapter that removes the pg_advisory_xact_lock, unsorts the product locks, and deletes the requestHash comparison - each has an existing test that should then fail.
summary: The best treatment of checkout reliability in the collection: a pg_advisory_xact_lock on (userId, requestId) taken before reading a durable userId_checkoutKey receipt, a payload fingerprint distinguishing a legitimate replay from a changed cart, product rows locked FOR UPDATE in sorted product-ID order to avoid deadlock, Prisma.Decimal money tested at the precision and total-bound edges, immutable order-line snapshots, and cancellation that restores inventory exactly once. All 80 checks (55 backend, 8 frontend, 3 setup, 14 Chromium) come from one run against a disposable PostgreSQL 18 cluster, including a genuine lost-response retry through the real UI. Difficulty is the issue: practice tasks ask for payment-adapter crash windows and quote expiry with review heuristics instead of answers - a capstone, not an entry point.

name: grokbuildhrproject
top_fix: Ship astraupskill/snapshots/leaveRoutes-before.ts.txt (the starter's `const { approverId, status } = req.body`) and astraupskill/evidence/, since 03-WORKED-CHANGE and VERIFICATION both make claims the learner cannot check from inside the repo; and either scope chartLock's hard-coded pg_advisory_xact_lock(74219801) to the affected chain or document that it globally serializes every employee write.
summary: Repairs the most instructive bug a junior can meet: the starter took approverId straight from the request body, so a caller could name themselves approver and overwrite a prior decision. The replacement derives the actor from the token, re-reads the reporting relationship from the database, blocks self-approval, and treats a decision as a version-conditional transition out of PENDING - with the course carefully separating the version rule from the state rule. The leave-overlap work is the standout: inclusive calendar semantics enforced twice, once in application code under an employee row lock and once by a PostgreSQL EXCLUDE USING gist partial constraint on daterange(start,end,'[]'). 76 checks backed by real reports; migration carries real CHECK constraints.

name: grokbuildmultitenantproject
top_fix: Rename or annotate checks/tenant-workspace/ so the authoritative run is obvious - the directory called final/ records two FAILING frontend tests while the green 55-check run is in verified/ - and add a paragraph to VERIFICATION.md narrating that earlier failure the way the rest of this batch does.
summary: The starter 'isolated' tenants with a comment and `req.headers['x-org-id'] || 'demo-org'`. The rebuild verifies an expiring token's algorithm/issuer/audience, looks up the caller's membership in the selected organization on every request, puts the organization predicate on every read and write, enforces the parent relationship again with a composite Task(projectId,organizationId) foreign key, and keeps version, audit and mutation in one transaction. Its 24 integration tests run real HTTP against disposable PostgreSQL and are named after properties - membership revocation without trusting old JWT roles, cross-tenant reads by a dual-member user, audit-failure rollback via a real trigger, competing writers at the same version - so the test file reads as a checklist. Practice tasks have acceptance criteria but no solutions.
